arxiv-1605-05080.title: Fermi-Pasta-Ulam recurrence and modulation instability
arxiv-1605-05080.creator: E.A. Kuznetsov
arxiv-1605-05080.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by E.A. Kuznetsov. We give a qualitative explanation of the analog of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam (FPU) recurrence in a one-dimensional focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation (NLSE). That recurrence can be considered as a result of the nonlinear development of modulation instability. All known exact localized solitons-type solutions describing propagation on the background of the modulationally unstable condensate show the recurrence to the condensate state after its interaction with solitons.

arxiv-2110-07024.title: \rheadt
arxiv-2110-07024.creator: Suhas Vijaykumar
arxiv-2110-07024.description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Suhas Vijaykumar. Abstract

This paper establishes non-asymptotic convergence of the cutoffs in Random serial dictatorship mechanism (RSD), in an environment with many students, many schools, and arbitrary student preferences. Convergence is shown to hold when the number of schools,
m
, and the number of students,
n
, satisfy the relation
m\ln m\ll n
, and we provide an example showing that this result is sharp.

arxiv-2212-01302.title: DeepFT: Fault-Tolerant Edge Computing using a Self-Supervised Deep Surrogate Model
arxiv-2212-01302.creator: Shreshth Tuli 1 , Giuliano Casale 1 , Ludmila Cherkasova 2 and Nicholas R. Jennings 3
arxiv-2212-01302.description: Abstract The emergence of latency-critical AI applications has been supported by the evolution of the edge computing paradigm. However, edge solutions are typically resource-constrained, posing reliability challenges due to heightened contention for compute and communication capacities and faulty application behavior in the presence of overload conditions.

arxiv-2303-03897.title: Primordial Gravitational Waves Assisted by Cosmological Scalar Perturbations
arxiv-2303-03897.creator: Yan-Heng Yu, Sai Wang
arxiv-2303-03897.description: Abstract Primordial gravitational waves are a crucial prediction of inflation theory, and their detection through their imprints on the cosmic microwave background is actively being pursued. However, these attempts have not yet been successful. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to detect primordial gravitational waves by searching for a signal of second-order tensor perturbations.

arxiv-2402-04362.title: Neural Networks Learn Statistics of Increasing Complexity
arxiv-2402-04362.creator: Nora Belrose, Quintin Pope, Lucia Quirke, Alex Mallen, Brennan Dury, Xiaoli Fern
arxiv-2402-04362.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nora Belrose, Quintin Pope, Lucia Quirke, Alex Mallen, Brennan Dury, Xiaoli Fern. The distributional simplicity bias (DSB) posits that neural networks learn low-order moments of the data distribution first, before moving on to higher-order correlations. In this work, we present compelling new evidence for the DSB by showing that networks automatically learn to perform well on maximum-entropy distributions whose low-order statistics match those of the training set early in training, then lose this ability later.

arxiv-2406-09116.title: Injective flows for star-like manifolds
arxiv-2406-09116.creator: Marcello Massimo Negri & Jonathan Aellen & Volker Roth
arxiv-2406-09116.description: Abstract Normalizing Flows (NFs) are powerful and efficient models for density estimation. When modeling densities on manifolds, NFs can be generalized to injective flows but the Jacobian determinant becomes computationally prohibitive. Current approaches either consider bounds on the log-likelihood or rely on some approximations of the Jacobian determinant.

arxiv-2408-11995.title: Compact Binary Merger Rate with Modified Gravity in Dark-Matter Spikes
arxiv-2408-11995.creator: Saeed Fakhry, Sara Gholamhoseinian, Marzieh Farhang
arxiv-2408-11995.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Saeed Fakhry, Sara Gholamhoseinian, Marzieh Farhang. In this study, we investigate the impact of modified gravity (MG) on the merger rate of compact binaries within dark-matter spikes surrounding super-massive black holes (SMBHs). Specifically, we calculate binary merger rates involving primordial black holes (PBHs) and/or neutron stars (NSs) in Hu-Sawicki f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) gravity and the normal branch of Dvali-Gabadadze-Porrati (nDGP) gravity, with three SMBH mass functions, Benson, Vika, and Shankar.

arxiv-2501-15546.title: Dispersive measurement of spin shot noise in a Bose–Einstein condensate
arxiv-2501-15546.creator: Kosuke Shibata, Naota Sekiguchi, Junnosuke Takai, Takuya Hirano
arxiv-2501-15546.description: Abstract We report dispersive spin shot noise measurement of a Bose–Einstein condensate (BEC). While dispersive probing has been used for quantum spin noise measurement of thermal and cold gases for decades, confirmative measurement of spin shot noise, i.e., the linear dependence of the spin variance on the number of atoms in a BEC has been lacking.

arxiv-2505-04009.title: Robust Variable Selection in High-dimensional Nonparametric Additive Model Journal: Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics
arxiv-2505-04009.creator: Suneel Babu Chatla and Abhijit Mandal
arxiv-2505-04009.description: Abstract Additive models belong to the class of structured nonparametric regression models that do not suffer from the curse of dimensionality. Finding the additive components that are nonzero when the true model is assumed to be sparse is an important problem, and it is well studied in the literature.

pmc-10477313.title: Simulating individual movement in fish
pmc-10477313.creator: Thomas W Pike, Oliver H P Burman
pmc-10477313.description: Accurately quantifying an animal’s movement is crucial for developing a greater empirical and theoretical understanding of its behaviour, and for simulating biologically plausible movement patterns. However, we have a relatively poor understanding of how animals move at fine temporal scales and in three-dimensional environments.

pmc-10738322.title: CONTRIBUTION OF CHRONIC CONDITIONS TO MORTALITY: DIFFERENCES BY RACE AND ETHNICITY
pmc-10738322.creator: Ana Quiñones, Miriam Elman, Gail McAvay, Brent Vander Wyk, Corey Nagel, Heather Allore

pmc-11663922.title: Effectiveness of spinal cord stimulation in diabetic patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia: small cohort study
pmc-11663922.creator: Anna E. Cyrek, Dietrich Koch, Arkadius Pacha, Sonia Radunz
pmc-11663922.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundChronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is the most severe form of peripheral artery disease (PAD). Patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) have a faster progression of PAD and a fourfold increased risk of CLTI compared to patients without DM. Epidural spinal cord stimulation (SCS) has been used as a method to improve microcirculation, relieve ischemic pain and reduce the number of amputations in patients with PAD.

pmc-12315758.title: FONDUE: Robust resolution-invariant denoising of MR images using Nested UNets
pmc-12315758.creator: Walter Adame-Gonzalez, Aliza Brzezinski-Rittner, Yashar Zeighami, M. Mallar Chakravarty, Reza Farivar, Mahsa Dadar
pmc-12315758.description: Recent human magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies continually push the boundaries of spatial resolution as a means to enhance levels of neuroanatomical detail and increase the accuracy and sensitivity of derived brain morphometry measures. However, acquisitions required to achieve these resolutions have a higher noise floor, potentially impacting segmentation and morphometric analysis results.

pmc-12447532.title: ExoTMS transcranial magnetic stimulation for the reduction of binge eating symptoms
pmc-12447532.creator: David Pánek, Toni Slavchev Donchev
pmc-12447532.description: AimTranscranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is an emerging treatment for binge eating (BE). TMS uses noninvasive magnetic pulses to stimulate the prefrontal cortex, which plays a role in decision‐making and self‐regulation. Early research suggests that TMS can reduce BE episodes by modulating brain activity linked to cravings and compulsive behavior.

pmc-12656082.title: IoTMindCare: An Integrative Reference Architecture for Safe and Personalized IoT-Based Depression Management
pmc-12656082.creator: Sanaz Zamani, Roopak Sinha, Samaneh Madanian, Minh Nguyen
pmc-12656082.description: Depression affects millions of people worldwide. Traditional management relies heavily on periodic clinical assessments and self-reports, which lack real-time responsiveness and personalization. Despite numerous research prototypes exploring Internet of Things (IoT)-based mental health support, almost none have translated into practical, mainstream solutions.

pmc-12690163.title: The Phylogenomic Framework and Infrageneric Classification of Temperate Asian Caraganeae (Leguminosae, Papilionoideae)
pmc-12690163.creator: Na Wang, Pei‐Liang Liu, Ling Zhang, Rui Ma, Liang Zhao, Hui Wang, Zhao‐Yang Chang
pmc-12690163.description: The legume tribe Caraganeae, consisting of the genera Caragana, Calophaca, and Halimodendron, is a mid‐sized, shrubby clade mainly found in temperate Central and Eastern Asia. Within this tribe, Caragana is the largest genus comprising 63–74 species, and it is recognized for its taxonomic complexity. However, the phylogenetic framework of Caraganeae and the infrageneric delimitations in Caragana remain inadequately resolved.

pmc-12749926.title: Synteny – a high throughput web tool to streamline causal gene prioritisation and provide insight into protein function
pmc-12749926.creator: Harry B Cutler, Jacqueline Stöckli, Søren Madsen, Stewart WC Masson, Oliver K Fuller, Tom Buckingham Shum, David E James
pmc-12749926.description: Accounting for human genetic evidence can improve the outcomes and impact of basic medical research studies. However, current approaches are incompatible with the high volume of disease-associated genes that require mechanistic interrogation and risk overlooking important phenotypic associations. Synteny responds to an urgent need in systems biology, scaling human genetic analysis to match the throughput of modern omics technologies.

pmc-13171557.title: Cognitive impairment and associated factors in elderly patients with schizophrenia: a retrospective observational study with phenotype analysis
pmc-13171557.creator: Yanping Cai, Yinxia Wu, Danjing Yao, Ying Xu
pmc-13171557.description: ObjectiveTo examine the prevalence of cognitive impairment and factors associated with cognitive impairment among elderly patients with schizophrenia, and to explore potential clinical phenotypes using a clustering approach.MethodsA retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted among 149 elderly inpatients with schizophrenia. Cognitive impairment was defined as Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score < 26.

pmc-13559814.title: Nonendoscopic Screening for Barrett’s Esophagus: Current Methods, Evidence, and Future Directions
pmc-13559814.creator: Ankoor H. Patel, Michael Ma, Petros C. Benias, Molly Stewart, Arvind J. Trindade
pmc-13559814.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The incidence of esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) has steadily risen over the past several decades. Screening for EAC and its metaplastic precursor, Barrett’s esophagus (BE), remains a challenge to prevent EAC development and decrease EAC-attributed mortality. Unfortunately, most BE is diagnosed at the time of diagnosis of EAC in the majority of patients with EAC, showcasing that current screening paradigms are neither widely accepted nor adequate.
